Berthline: three starter directions

/omni:pixel-perfect init, starter path, on a repository with no design system. Each direction is a full set: 30 semantic tokens in light and dark, eight parts in every state, and the two reference screens built only from them. The product's answers come from its README and design form: the harbourmaster at a desk by the window, skippers on a phone in full sun or at dusk, a shipping-forecast voice. Faces are named first in each font-family and not loaded: the browser's fallbacks stand in. Example data throughout.

A · Chart room

An Admiralty chart on the desk: chart paper, navy ink, chart magenta for focus, a serif for titles and figures set like a tide table. Dense enough for the harbourmaster's whole pontoon at once, and dark ink on paper in full sun.

Drawn from: the Met Office forecast the README admires (plain, dense, read the same way by all), the desk by the window and the phone in full sun. Faces: IBM Plex Mono, IBM Plex Sans, Source Serif 4. Corners 2px, controls 40px high. 30 semantic tokens, light then dark in each pair below; every text pair passes 4.5:1 and every edge 3:1 in both.

B · Pontoon

Built for the pontoon in glare: white and black, a signal yellow for the one action, condensed capitals and 52 px targets for wet hands. Loud on the desk too.

Drawn from: the skipper on the pontoon in full sun with wet hands. Faces: Archivo, Archivo Narrow. Corners 0px, controls 52px high. 30 semantic tokens, light then dark in each pair below; every text pair passes 4.5:1 and every edge 3:1 in both.

C · Harbour office

A calm office tool: a sea-green action on cool grey, soft corners and room to breathe. Easy on the eye all day at the desk.

Drawn from: the harbourmaster's long day at the desk. Faces: Source Sans 3. Corners 8px, controls 44px high. 30 semantic tokens, light then dark in each pair below; every text pair passes 4.5:1 and every edge 3:1 in both.

Checked before showing

Craft floor's refuse list: no card grid as the page, no hero metric, no kicker, no gradient text, no glass, no coloured side border, no hard offset shadow, no glyph standing in for an icon, monospace only for berth codes, lengths and times (data, not costume). Light is the default because both scenes are in daylight; dark is for dusk. The word pass and the parts check run on every marked screen.
